excluded_seen: The wider screen (examples/scale-up-search/rivals.py): the 1,196 different rules of the even draw's numbers 1 to 1,200, each against its copy from start 11001. Both cuts were read off it: the first off its first 458 rules, where it then held on the other 738; the second off all 1,196. The bounds here were set between what it gave and what would mean nothing.

The sizing look (sizing.py): the first 200 of those rules again from start 11002, to learn how far a rule's verdict hangs on its start: 199 held territories or not as they had from 11001. It tested no rule that the screen had not.

The rest of the search: the one-species screen of the same 1,196 rules and of 172 near-majority rules, 450 soups, the contests of 29 rules and of the 18 rules one count from B2378/S25678, and the large-grid runs. No rule of any of them is among the 600: `seen()` lists them and `fresh()` leaves them out.

No rule of this test (the draw's numbers 1,201 on) has been drawn into a run, and no run has begun from start 14001. The rules' counts were read to size the test: how many rules fall in each group is in `design`.

further_rules.why: the second cut is judged on every rule that needs two or three of its own kind for a birth, among the 600 and among the 1,200 fresh rules drawn after them

body.holds_territories: in at least one of a rule's four contests: both species hold a cell in twenty or more at the end, their block counts go against each other (-0.5 or under at blocks of 32), and one has a correlation area of 16 cells or more there
body.not_tested: a claim whose group has fewer rules than its `needs`
body.source: docs/scale-up-plan.md, step 4b and decision D9; examples/scale-up-search/rivals.py
body.statement: 600 fresh rules of the even draw, each as two species with the one rule on a wrapped square grid of side 256 for 512 generations, from a full start and a half-full one, under the random draw and under the standoff, and each alone; and for the second cut, the rules that need two or three for a birth among 1,200 more. The share of rules that hold territories against their copy goes with how few of its own kind a cell needs to be born (few at none, most often at two or three, hardly any at four or more), and among the rules that need two or three, with whether a cell can last on one or two of its own kind. Rules that hold under one tie-break only do so mostly under the standoff, and a rule that organises itself alone is no likelier to hold territories.
